decisions.issues: Framing does not match the script: the troop fills the foreground at medium-close range, with Raza Khan large in the left third, when the cold-open wide shot needs them small and far down the beach riding toward us. It also steals the arrival beat of 1.4. The fourth rider (about x 0.55, y 0.5) holds a malformed crossbar or forked stick beside his lance. The most distant horses read as pale grey in the haze. Otherwise good: the dawn sun over the palms on the laterite bluff, the sea on the right, the shining low-tide sand, white jamas and turbans, a single green turban, and open sky for the caption.
decisions.correction: CORRECTION: The troop must be FAR down the beach and SMALL. Show a column of about twenty riders, two or three abreast, riding head-on toward the camera along the wet sand. The column takes up only the middle third of the frame width, and no rider is taller than about one sixth of the frame height; the nearest rider is still at least a hundred paces away. The whole foreground is empty, shining wet sand reflecting the dawn sky, with no figure near the camera. Keep what worked: the dawn sun just clearing the coconut palms on the low laterite bluff at left, the sea and surf at right, the tin-bright low-tide sand, the white jamas and high-wrapped white turbans, a single tiny deep-green turban at the head of the column, and open pale sky across the upper part of the frame. Each rider holds exactly one plain upright bamboo lance with a simple iron head: no bows, crossbars, forked sticks or second weapons. Every horse, including the most distant, is dark bay, dark brown or black, and none reads as grey.

decisions.issues: A European church with a bell tower and a cross stands on a fortified stone bastion on the far shore. That is a European building that does not belong on this beach. The foreground leg is a shapeless club with no readable fetlock or pastern. With the tail and hind legs filling the upper left, it does not clearly read as a foreleg planted at the wet margin. The rendering is also nearly photographic, not the inked style of 1.1.
decisions.correction: CORRECTION: The background must be an empty, natural Malabar shore and nothing else: shining low-tide wet sand, low surf, and a low laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms. Put NO church, chapel, fort, bastion, wall, tower, cross, building, ship or person anywhere in the frame. Show ONE dark-bay FORELEG in clear, correct anatomy, seen from the side and slightly in front at hoof level, with the knee, cannon bone, fetlock joint and pastern all readable. The hoof is sunk in grey slurry up to the pastern so the hoof itself is hidden, wet sand wells up around it, and a thin sheet of foam slides in from the right. Any other legs may show only as soft, out-of-focus shapes behind it, with no tail in the frame. Use the inked graphic-novel style of panel 1.1 (clean ink line, painted colour, warm low dawn light), not photorealism. Leave open pale sky across the upper part of the frame for the caption.

decisions.issues: The background is a crenellated stone fort wall instead of the open beach, so the setting does not match 1.1 or the script. The panel is rendered as a photograph, clashing with the inked style of the page. A rider's eyes peer over the horse's head, which is more than the out-of-focus edge of a turban. The eye beat itself is good: a real dark-bay eye rolled back with the white showing, and no human expression.
decisions.correction: CORRECTION: Set the panel on the open beach, not at a fort. Behind the horse's head show only pale dawn sky, a few coconut palms on a low laterite bluff, and perhaps a sliver of sea. Put NO stone wall, battlement, rampart or building anywhere. Draw it in the same inked graphic-novel style as panels 1.1 and 1.4 (clean ink line, painted colour, warm dawn light), not as a photograph. Keep what worked: a tight close-up of a dark-bay horse's eye rolled back with the white showing, a real horse's eye with no human expression, a plain leather bridle, the edge of a quilted saddle, and at upper left the soft, out-of-focus edge of a high-wrapped white turban and a bamboo lance shaft. Show only that turban edge: no rider's face, eyes or skin. Keep the upper right of the frame as open sky for the two captions.

decisions.issues: The setting is a harbour, not the empty beach of 1.1. It shows European sailing ships offshore, a European hilltop fort and town, a stone building at the right edge, and a European soldier in a morion helmet with a bystander, barrels and coiled rope in the right foreground. Raza Khan himself is on model (olive-green turban, green drape, goatee, pointed moustache, scar on his anatomical left cheek), and the white-turbaned troop on dark horses is right.
decisions.correction: CORRECTION: This is an open, empty Malabar beach at dawn and nothing else: shining low-tide wet sand, the sea and surf on one side, and a low laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms on the other. Put NO ships or sails on the sea, NO fort, castle, walls, stone buildings or town on the shore, NO European soldiers, helmets or breastplates, and NO barrels, crates, rope or bystanders in the foreground. The only people in the frame are Raza Khan and his Madurai riders. Keep what worked: Raza Khan in the centre on his dark-bay horse, with his olive-green high-wrapped turban, the green drape over his white jama, goatee and pointed moustache, and the scar on his anatomical left cheek (our right). Behind him, the riders in white jamas and high-wrapped white turbans hold bamboo lances without pennons on dark horses, with open pale sky across the upper third. Raza Khan salutes: the lance held upright in his right fist with the shaft drawn in against his chest, his eyes level toward the camera, which stands where Nagoji waits.

decisions.issues: This is the wrong scene. It shows a Portuguese fort courtyard with morion-helmeted, breastplated European soldiers guarding ragged prisoners, stone walls, an arch, European ships and a hilltop castle; the captivity panel and fort backdrop on the reference sheet leaked in. Nagoji is seen mostly from behind, so this is not the reverse-angle first full view of him weighing the troop. His turban, curls, tunic, sash, boots, talwar, moustache, clean chin and the grey are otherwise close to model. His ear ornament is a hanging gold drop (noted only, not a rejection reason).
decisions.correction: CORRECTION: Set the panel on the same open Malabar beach at dawn as panels 1.1 and 1.4: shining low-tide wet sand, the sea behind him, and a low laterite bluff with coconut palms. Include NO fort, stone walls, arches, towers, ships or crates, NO Portuguese or European soldiers, helmets or breastplates, and NO prisoners in rags. The only other figures are the soft, out-of-focus backs or shoulders of two or three Madurai riders in white jamas and high-wrapped white turbans at the near frame edge: the troop he faces. Use a reverse angle from among the troop: Nagoji seen from the front in three-quarter view, mounted on a plain light-grey horse, his face fully visible, his eyes on the riders just past the camera, not on us, cool and appraising. Keep what worked: the rust-red turban with curls at the nape, the cream tunic with sleeves down to his wrists, the broad red sash over the shoulder and knotted at the waist, cream trousers, boots, the talwar at his hip, the thick curled moustache and clean-shaven chin, the grey's padded, quilted Indian cloth saddle and plain bridle, and the inked graphic-novel style. Keep the upper part of the frame as open pale sky for the caption.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Ponnan matches the bible and script: bare-headed, short curly hair, thick moustache, clean chin, dark-brown short jacket, red cloth over his anatomical right shoulder, white mundu hitched with bare knees, on a small dun pony. The Maravar line is bare-headed in short jackets and white mundus, ponies dun and dark brown, no greys. Low angle up at a laterite bluff. Small points: the distant background to the right shows an inland lagoon and hills rather than palms on the bluff; Ponnan and the riders have shoes in their stirrups; one background rider has a beard. Open sky at upper left and upper right takes both captions without covering any face.

Varma and Ramayyan are close to the bible: no turban, a forehead mark, bare chest, a cream-and-gold cloth, gold necklaces, spear leaning on the pole; Ramayyan is thin and balding, in white, with palm leaves and a stylus. But the beat and setting are wrong. 1) This is a medium shot with the two men large in the foreground, not a long shot of two small figures through heat haze, and there is no haze. 2) The awning stands on two or three poles, not one. 3) The beach below is filled with an invented infantry army: long ranks of foot soldiers with round shields and spears. Nothing in this chapter shows that, and it clashes with the cavalry exercise on panels 1.1, 2.1 and 2.4. No Madurai horse or Maravar line appears. Minor: Varma's knot sits at the back of his crown rather than above his left ear.
decisions.correction: Make this a true long shot through heat haze: visible shimmering haze rises off the sand in the foreground, and the awning with its two seated figures is SMALL, together no more than a quarter of the frame height, set in the right third on the lower shoulder of the laterite bluff. The awning is a single cloth stretched from ONE wooden pole, with Varma's spear leaning against that pole. Keep both looks exactly. Varma: bare-headed, no turban, black hair in a knot above his left ear, simple Vaishnavite forehead lines, bare chest, one cream-and-gold cloth over the shoulder, gold necklaces. Ramayyan: thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle in his lap, stylus ready. The beach below must hold NO foot soldiers, NO shields, NO infantry ranks or parade lines. Show only, small and far off on the wet sand, a few Madurai horsemen in white jamas and white turbans on dark horses, and a little along the bluff from the awning the edge of the line of bare-headed Maravar riders on small dun and dark-brown ponies. Keep the open sky at upper left clear for the caption.

decisions.issues: The over-the-shoulder insert works well: rust-red turban, cream sleeve pushed to the elbow, left hand on the reins of the grey, red sash as on the commander sheet, talwar hilt, and plain sand at upper right for the captions. Two failures. 1) The brand is drawn as raised cursive letter-shapes that read like a word (roughly 'Pett'): pseudo-text, the opposite of 'blurred past reading'. 2) Nagoji's jaw and chin carry clear stubble, but the commander look requires a clean-shaven chin. Note only: his ear ornament is a hanging gold drop.
decisions.correction: The brand must not look like writing in any way. Draw it as one irregular, blotchy patch of pale, shiny, puckered burn-scar tissue about the size of a large coin on the inner left forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, with uneven raised welts that merge into each other. No separate strokes, loops, letter shapes, cursive forms, numerals or cross that could be read as script. Nagoji's jaw and chin are completely clean-shaven: smooth skin with no stubble and no beard shadow, only the thick curled moustache. Keep everything else as it is: the high over-the-shoulder angle, the rust-red turban, curly hair at the nape, the cream sleeve pushed back to the elbow, the healed, ridged nails, the left hand on the reins of the plain grey, the red sash, the talwar hilt, and the plain sand in the upper right for the two captions.

decisions.issues: Staging is right: three abreast with Raza on the left, Nagoji in the centre pointing with his right arm, and Ponnan on the right, lower on his dun pony. Nagoji is on model: rust-red turban, clean chin, curled moustache, cream tunic, red sash, boots, grey horse (his ear ornament is a hanging drop, noted only). Three failures. 1) A European-style stone fortress with a white domed bell-tower sits on the headland at upper right: a European building the prompt does not name, and not the palm-crowned laterite bluff of this beach. 2) Raza Khan's scar is on his ANATOMICAL RIGHT cheek. His face is turned to our right, and the scar is on the near cheek beside his visible ear. 3) Ponnan's jacket lapel carries painted pseudo-lettering (letter-like gold marks running down the lapel), and the jacket reads as a buttoned, lapelled Western shirt.
decisions.correction: Remove the fortress: no fort, castle, tower, church, wall or masonry building anywhere. The headland behind is only a low laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms above the sea. Raza Khan's scar must be on his ANATOMICAL LEFT cheek. Turn his head slightly toward our left, the way Nagoji is pointing down the beach, so his left cheek faces us and the puckered scar sits on the cheek on OUR RIGHT side of his face. Ponnan's short dark-brown jacket is a plain, collarless Indian riding jacket with no lapels and no buttons, and no embroidery, trim, marks or anything letter-like on the cloth. Keep everything else: the three riders abreast, Nagoji centred on the tall grey pointing down the beach with his right arm, rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, Raza on the left in the deep-green turban on the dark bay, Ponnan on the right, bare-headed with the red cloth over his right shoulder, lower on the small dun pony, and the open sky across the top for the two balloons.

decisions.issues: Raza Khan himself is on model: frowning, scar on his anatomical left cheek toward us, deep-green turban, pointed moustache with his sheet's goatee, white jama, hand on the hilt, dark-bay horse. The background breaks several chapter rules. 1) The Madurai troop behind him wear GREEN turbans and green shoulder drapes, but the troop must be in white or off-white turbans, with Raza the only green turban. 2) A red banner with a white conch (the Travancore standard) flies among the Madurai lances, but their lances carry no pennons or banners. 3) A white European-style church and fort stand on the far headland at left.
decisions.correction: The Madurai riders behind Raza Khan wear knee-length white jamas with plain waistbands and high-wrapped WHITE or off-white turbans, never green, and no green shoulder drapes. Raza Khan's turban is the ONLY green in the troop. Their long bamboo lances carry no pennons, flags or banners: remove the red conch banner entirely. Remove the white church and the fort on the headland. The background is only the beach, the sea and a low laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms, with no buildings of any kind. Keep Raza Khan exactly as drawn: frowning, scar on his anatomical left cheek toward us, deep-green high-wrapped turban, pointed moustache, white jama, one hand resting on his pommel, on his dark-bay horse, with open sky above and beside his head for the two balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): Nagoji himself is good. He has the rust-red turban with curls at the nape, a clean chin with only light shading, the thick curled moustache, the cream tunic, the broad red sash, boots and talwar, and he sits on a plain dappled grey. His ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop; noted only, not a reason to reject. The setting is wrong, and this rejects it. He sits on a stone rampart, with a Portuguese-style fort and a domed sentry turret (garita) behind him. On the far headland is a white European town with a church bell tower, and the shore is rocky. This should be the open wet-sand Travancore beach where the drill takes place, matching 2.4 and 3.4. European buildings are forbidden in this chapter.
decisions.correction: Setting correction: Nagoji sits level on the plain grey gelding on the open, flat wet-sand beach of the Travancore coast. Behind him is a bright sea with low surf breaking on smooth sand, and to one side the low red-laterite bluff topped with coconut palms. This is the same beach as the cavalry drill in the neighbouring panels. Draw NO stone fort, ramparts, battlements, parapet wall, domed sentry turret, church, bell tower, cross, white-walled town or any building anywhere, and no rocky shoreline. Keep Nagoji exactly as in the previous attempt: face, rust-red turban with curls at the nape, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar at the hip, left hand on the reins. Keep the plain grey horse in the left foreground. Keep the large clear sky in the upper right for one speech balloon, away from his face.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): Raza Khan's head is right. He has the olive-green high-wrapped turban, hawk nose, pointed moustache and grey-streaked goatee, a scar on his ANATOMICAL LEFT cheek facing the camera, a tight jaw, and eyes flicking up and away. The background breaks the script and the continuity with 2.2. The king does not sit under a one-pole cloth awning on a low stool. Instead he sits on a throne on a red-draped dais under a four-pole fringed canopy, wearing a crown or turban-like headdress and a robe, flanked by standing spear guards. Ramayyan is absent. In the lower right, several Madurai troopers stand on foot with crossed leather belts, and some wear GREEN turbans (only Raza may wear green). A thin black frame line is painted around the image.
decisions.correction: Background correction: above and behind Raza Khan's shoulder, small and hazy on the low shoulder of a red-laterite bluff above the beach, draw a single plain cloth awning. It has ONE upright pole with the cloth slung from it: no four-pole canopy, no fringe or tassels, no dais, no throne, no carpet, no standing guards. Under it sit two tiny figures on low stools. One is Marthanda Varma, bare-headed with his hair in a knot above his left ear, no turban, no crown, no crest, bare-chested, with a cream-and-gold cloth over one shoulder and his spear leaning against the pole. The other is Ramayyan, thin, in plain white cloth, with palm leaves in his lap. Remove the foot soldiers in the lower right. If any Madurai riders appear, they are mounted, in white jamas and WHITE or off-white turbans only, with no other green turban and no crossed belts. Hint at the open beach and sea beyond. Draw no border or frame line around the image. Keep Raza Khan's head and shoulders exactly as in the previous attempt: olive-green high-wrapped turban, hawk nose, pointed moustache and goatee, scar on his anatomical left cheek toward the camera, tight jaw, eyes flicking up and away. Keep clear sky top left and top right for two lettering areas.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): Raza Khan is right in his green turban, white jama, scar on the anatomical left cheek and dark-bay horse, seen from behind as he wheels away and looks back over his left shoulder, though his lips are closed rather than calling. It is rejected because a European fortress stands on the headland behind him: walls, red-tiled white houses and a church bell tower with a cross. The inset has three more problems. Ponnan's Maravar stand ON FOOT with spears, and many wear red sashes, when only Ponnan wears red and the Maravar are mounted on dun and dark-brown ponies. Ponnan's own horse is a dark bay with a white star, not the small dun pony of 2.1 and 2.4. His red cloth hangs over both shoulders like a stole, not over his right shoulder. Ponnan's face, curly hair, moustache, brown jacket, faint smile and raised signalling hand are good.
decisions.correction: Correction: the coastline behind Raza Khan is the open Travancore beach only: wet sand, surf, coconut palms and the red-laterite bluff. Draw NO fort, walls, houses, red-tiled roofs, church, bell tower, cross or any building anywhere. Raza Khan's lips are parted as he calls back over his shoulder. In the upper-corner inset, Ponnan sits on a SMALL rough-coated DUN pony with no white face markings, matching the earlier panels. His single narrow red cloth crosses over his RIGHT shoulder only. Behind him on the bluff, his Maravar are MOUNTED on small dun and dark-brown ponies (no greys). They are bare-headed, in plain white or undyed mundus hitched for riding and short dark jackets, with no red cloth on anyone but Ponnan. Keep everything else from the previous attempt: Raza Khan from behind on his dark-bay horse with the quilted saddle, olive-green turban, white jama, green shoulder drape, scar on his anatomical left cheek visible as he looks back. In the inset, keep Ponnan's face, short curly hair, thick moustache, clean chin, dark-brown jacket, faint smile and raised open hand. Keep clear sky in the upper right for one speech balloon.

decisions.issues: Acceptable with minor notes. Raza Khan leads in the single deep-green turban (scar on his anatomical left cheek, goatee, lance). The Madurai line wears white jamas and white turbans, on dark bay, brown and black horses (no greys) with quilted saddles and pennonless lances, spray flying. The bare-headed Maravar stream down the bluff on brown and dun ponies. There are no buildings, no text and no gore. Minor deviations: the troopers wear crossed leather chest straps and leather belts rather than plain cloth waistbands (they still read as Carnatic cavalry, not Travancore regulars). Several horses carry small white stars. Most Maravar are bare-chested rather than in short jackets. The line is already in the shallows rather than just reaching the waterline. The clear sky in the upper left takes the caption.

v01 (the only candidate): Raza Khan faces the viewer's right with his ear toward the viewer's left, and his scar sits on the cheek nearest the camera. That is his ANATOMICAL RIGHT cheek, so the scar is on the wrong side, which breaks the bible and the chapter check. The script beat is also weak. The Madurai horses are galloping forward in stride through splashing mud, a charge rather than a flounder: no horse is visibly sunk, none is trying to turn, the lances stay upright and the line has not become a knot. The distant headland carries a stone fort or tower that matches neither the laterite bluff with coconut palms in 3.4 nor the script. What works: white jamas and white turbans, dark bay, brown and black horses, quilted saddles, bamboo lances without pennons, the bare-headed rider on the dun pony at right grinning back over his shoulder while it throws sand and darts away, and clear sky at the upper right for the caption. No painted text, no gore, no hand faults found.
decisions.correction: Keep v01's layout and palette: the knot of Madurai riders filling the left two-thirds, the bare-headed Maravar rider on the dun pony at the right edge grinning back over his shoulder as it darts clear in a fan of wet sand, and open sky across the upper right for the caption. Fix Raza Khan's scar. Turn his face toward the viewer's LEFT so his ANATOMICAL LEFT cheek is the one nearest the camera, and put the scar on that cheek only, with no mark on his right cheek. Keep his deep-green high-wrapped turban, green shoulder drape, hawk nose and pointed moustache. Show the failure instead of a charge: the heavy horses are sunk past the fetlocks almost to the knees in grey slurry, their bodies twisted mid-turn with haunches dropped, heads thrown up and legs scrabbling for footing; one bamboo lance tips steeply sideways; riders lean back and haul on the reins; the line has collapsed into a tangled, bunched knot. No horse falls or is hurt. Behind the beach, show only the low laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms from the previous page, with no fort, tower, ruin or building anywhere.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): wrong setting. The panel is set on a dry, dusty inland plain with grass tufts, scattered rocks and a crenellated stone hill fort. There is no wet sand, no sea and no laterite bluff, so it breaks continuity with 3.4, 4.1 and 4.3, which are all at the water's edge, and it contradicts Nagoji's line about this earth judging weight. Nagoji's mouth is closed or barely parted, so he does not read as calling to both lines. What works: Nagoji matches the commander sheet (rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin), with his arm out between a white-turbaned Madurai line on dark horses and a bare-headed Maravar line on dun and brown ponies, a plain grey horse and good open sky for the balloon. Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a stud.
decisions.correction: Keep v01's composition and costumes exactly: Nagoji centred on his plain grey with his right arm flung out, the white-turbaned, white-jama Madurai riders on dark bay, brown and black horses on the left, the bare-headed Maravar in dark-brown jackets and white mundus on dun and brown ponies on the right, and open sky across the top for the balloon. Change the setting to the same Malabar beach as the neighbouring panels: low tide, a broad plain of packed wet sand with shallow sheets of water and grey slurry around the hooves, the Arabian Sea and white surf behind, and the low laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms along one side. No dry earth, grass tufts, scrub, boulders, fort, tower or building of any kind. The Madurai horses are mud-spattered to the belly and their line is still ragged from the failed turn. Nagoji's mouth is clearly open as he calls out to both lines, head turned slightly toward the Madurai riders.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate): anachronism. Ponnan wears a modern collared, button-front shirt under his jacket, with a metal zip pull clearly drawn at the top of the placket (about x 0.67, y 0.51), which is a 20th-century fastening. The background riders at the left wear red waist sashes, and the script says only Ponnan wears red; this is minor. Everything else works: Nagoji in the near foreground on the tall plain grey in the full commander look (rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin); Ponnan beyond him and a head lower on a small dun pony, bare-headed with short curly hair, a thick moustache and a clean chin, broad and stocky, red cloth over his right shoulder, white mundu, bare legs, eyes forward; a shoreline setting; and wide clear sky at the upper right and upper centre for both balloons. Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a stud.
decisions.correction: Keep v01 exactly: framing, both riders, their faces and poses, Nagoji's commander costume on the tall plain grey in the near foreground, Ponnan a head lower beyond him on the small dun pony with eyes forward, the shoreline and the open sky across the upper right. Change only Ponnan's upper garment. He wears a single short, collarless, open-fronted dark-brown cotton jacket over his BARE chest, with no shirt beneath, no collar, no buttons, no zip, no metal fastenings or clasps of any kind; the narrow red cloth stays over his right shoulder. The distant riders at the left are Maravar in plain white or undyed mundus and dark jackets with no red sashes or red cloth, because only Ponnan wears red.

decisions.issues: The setting is wrong. Instead of the chapter's Malabar beach (low-tide wet sand and surf, as in 4.1, 4.3 and 5.2 to 5.4), the panel shows an inland dirt track lined with ruined stone walls, a rocky Deccan hilltop fortress and dry scrub, with the sea only a distant strip. Ponnan is off-model: his face is lean and long, his loose curls fall long like Nagoji's, he has an upturned curled moustache and gold earrings. He no longer has the sheet's broad round face, short cropped curls and heavy straight moustache (compare 4.3), so he reads as Nagoji's twin. The background beat is also missing: Raza Khan rides toward the camera shouting and gesturing at the viewer, not cursing at his horse, and his horse is clean and dry, not fresh from the slurry. What works: Nagoji's commander look (rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, red sash, boots, talwar, clean chin) on the plain grey; Ponnan's dark-brown jacket, red cloth on his anatomical right shoulder, white mundu, bare legs, dun pony a head lower, eyes slid toward Raza; padded cloth saddles; clear sky top centre and right for two balloons. Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud.
decisions.correction: Setting and cast correction: this is the same narrow Malabar beach as the rest of the chapter, at low tide. Underfoot is flat wet grey-tan sand with puddles and hoof-churned slurry, the Arabian Sea surf runs behind, and a low red laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms rises at one side. There are no stone walls or ruins, no dirt track, no rocky Deccan hills, and no hilltop fort, fortress, tower or building anywhere. Ponnan must keep his sheet's face: a broad, round, heavy-jawed face, short tight curls cropped close to the head, a thick straight heavy moustache, no earrings, and a visibly stockier build than Nagoji. He must not resemble Nagoji. In the background, small, Raza Khan sits his dark-bay horse just out of the slurry, the horse's legs caked in wet sand. He looks DOWN at the horse's head and neck, scolding it with one hand raised, and does not look toward the camera or the other riders. Keep everything else that worked: Nagoji nearest the camera on the plain grey in rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar; Ponnan a head lower on the small dun pony in a plain dark-brown jacket, narrow red cloth on his right shoulder and white mundu with bare legs, in three-quarter view with only his eyes slid sideways toward Raza Khan; padded Indian cloth saddles; and open sky in the upper part of the frame for two balloons.

decisions.issues: The background Madurai riders wear GREEN turbans and green shoulder drapes. That breaks the troop rule (white or off-white turbans only; Raza Khan alone in green). On the right horizon there are three European square-rigged sailing ships and a European-style fort with a tower, which the prompt does not name, so this is an anachronism and continuity break. What works: Raza Khan matches his sheet (deep-green turban, hawk nose, pointed moustache, goatee, scar on his anatomical left cheek with his face turned to frame-left). He sits a quilted cloth saddle on a dark-bay horse on wet sand, shaking clods from his boot in the iron stirrup, with clear sky across the top for two balloons.
decisions.correction: Background correction: the riders behind Raza Khan are the Madurai troop. Every one of them wears a high-wrapped WHITE or off-white turban and a plain white knee-length jama with a plain cloth waistband. There are NO green turbans, no green shoulder drapes and no green cloth on anyone but Raza Khan, who is the only man in green. Remove the sailing ships and the fort tower on the right. The sea horizon is empty, and the shore is only the Malabar beach with coconut palms on a low red laterite bluff. There are no ships, masted boats, forts, towers or buildings of any kind anywhere in the frame. Keep everything else that worked: Raza Khan on his dark-bay horse on the wet sand, face turned toward the left of the frame so his scarred left cheek shows, pointed moustache, deep-green turban, white jama, quilted Indian cloth saddle with a plain iron stirrup, furiously shaking clods of wet sand from his boot; and the clear sky across the upper part of the frame for two balloons.

decisions.issues: On the headland stands a whitewashed European-style fortress with bastions, a sentry turret and a flagpole. That is a European building the prompt does not name. decisions.correction: Show Nagoji alone in frame, squatting low on his heels on the broad flat of packed wet sand exactly as in the water-pause panel before it (Raza Khan is just off panel), turned three-quarter toward the camera and talking, one hand raised in a small explaining gesture. decisions.correction: Keep Raza Khan exactly as drawn: facing left, wiping his brow with the tail of his deep-green turban cloth, scarred left cheek and mouth uncovered, pointed moustache, white jama, green drape, open sky above-left for the two lettering areas. decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate): the content is right. decisions.correction: Render this in the same inked graphic-novel illustration style as the rest of Chapter 7 and its panel 6.5: confident black ink linework with painted colour, the warm tan wet-sand palette of 6.5, and no photographic texture, real-photo shells or depth-of-field blur. Keep the content that worked: a square, edge-to-edge overhead view of shining wet sand. One single straight groove runs horizontally across the middle of the square, with the tip of a slim grey driftwood stick still in it at its left end. Only one fingertip shows on the stick at the left frame edge, with no forearm. Add a few grains and one small lip of foam at a corner, and no other marks. decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate): the beat is roughly there: an overhead view of wet sand with a straight groove and two curved grooves that bend toward it and hook away, made by a driftwood stick with only a fingertip showing, and no text. decisions.correction: Render this in the same inked graphic-novel illustration style as the rest of Chapter 7 and its panel 6.5: black ink linework with painted colour, the warm tan wet-sand palette of 6.5, and no photographic texture or photo shells. Match the previous inset exactly: a square, edge-to-edge overhead view with the same single straight groove running horizontally across the middle of the square. Add two curved grooves, one above the line and one below it, each a long, shallow, plain arc. Each sweeps in from that side's outer end, bends toward the straight groove, then turns gently away before touching it, ending in a soft rounded tip. decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate): the composition is good. Nagoji crouches on the left with the stick and Raza Khan on the right, facing left with his scarred left cheek toward camera. Nagoji's sleeves are rolled up to mid-forearm with both forearms bare, against the note that his sleeves come down to his wrists. His footwear also looks like modern lace-up boots. Raza's turban rises close to the upper-right corner, where the 6.4 inset will sit. Ear ornament: a small hanging gold drop rather than a stud (noted only).
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Nagoji crouched on the left scoring the sand with a slim driftwood stick, and Raza Khan crouched on the right facing Nagoji so his scarred left cheek faces the camera. Keep both faces clear below their turbans, the open sea and sky across the upper third, and the thin sheet of foam softening the near end of the straight groove. Fix the drawing in the sand. It is exactly three grooves and nothing else: one straight groove running from near to far, and two long, shallow, plain curved grooves, one on each side. Each curve bends toward the straight groove and turns gently away before touching it, and every groove end is a soft rounded stop. No arrowheads, barbs, triangular or pointed tips, crossbars, diagonal strokes or any other marks. Nagoji's cream sleeves come all the way down to his wrists on both arms, with no bare forearms. He wears tall soft leather riding boots as on his sheet, not lace-up shoes. Keep both turbans within the middle 60 percent of the frame width, so that the square insets set in the upper left and upper right corners do not clip them.

decisions.issues: Clean on cast and beat: Raza Khan crouched over the sand grooves with his anatomical-left scar toward camera, Nagoji with forearms on knees, clean chin and curled moustache. At least four background Madurai riders wear green turbans, which breaks the bible rule that Raza Khan alone wears green and the troop wear white or off-white. decisions.correction: Set this on the same wet beach as panels 6.5 and 7.1: packed wet sand at the water's edge, the half-erased driftwood grooves and a thin sheet of foam near Raza Khan's feet, black laterite rocks, the sea behind, a low bluff with coconut palms. Keep Raza Khan in the left foreground exactly as drawn (deep-green high-wrapped turban, olive-green drape over a white jama, scar on his anatomical LEFT cheek toward camera, pointed moustache, grey-flecked goatee), but catch him mid-rise from his crouch: one knee still bent, one hand pushing off it, no spear in hand, eyes out on the horses on the flat. Every other rider in the background wears a high-wrapped WHITE or off-white turban and a white jama, on dark bay, dark brown or black horses. There are NO other green turbans anywhere in the frame. decisions.issues: A white lighthouse tower stands on the headland, an anachronism and a European building, alongside ruined towers and buildings along the bluff. decisions.correction: Remove the white lighthouse and every building, tower, fort or ruin from the headland. Render in the same inked graphic-novel line art with flat watercolour colour as panels 7.1 and 7.4, not a photographic painting. Show the line actually wheeling: the whole mixed line bends through one clean, continuous arc at the water's edge, the leading riders already turned back toward the sand on the near side, and a single arc of thrown spray follows the curve behind them. decisions.correction: Set this panel on the open, rocky, sandy top of the coastal bluff beside the simple one-pole cloth awning seen in panel 7.4, with the training beach, the bright strip of sea and palms below and behind under a clear afternoon sky. Keep both figures exactly as they were drawn in the previous attempt: Ramayyan's thin face, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, and the blank, edge-on palm-leaf bundle and stylus; Nagoji's rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, tiny flush gold ear stud, cream tunic with red sash, and talwar. decisions.correction: Keep both cream tunic sleeves rolled down to the wrists so that neither forearm shows any bare skin. Draw no scar, brand, pale patch or crossed lines on either arm. decisions.issues: Acceptable, with minor notes. decisions.correction: Keep both cream tunic sleeves rolled down to the wrists so no forearm skin shows on either arm, with no scar, brand or pale patch anywhere on his arms. In the picket line, show only dark bay, dark brown and black tall horses and small dun or dark brown ponies, with at most one plain grey (his gelding) and no other grey or white horse anywhere, including by the tents and the fires. Keep everything else exactly as it is: the dusk sky and palms, the cook fires in the dark beyond, Nagoji's pose and full commander costume (rust-red turban, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar) with his hand on the black horse, the riderless, saddleless, bridleless black mare at full stretch across black Deccan soil bleeding in from the right edge like a stain, and the clear sky across the top for two captions.

decisions.issues: Kayal herself is close to the sheet: an ochre red-brown bay with black mane, tail and lower legs, ears forward, head a little high, looking at the viewer, standing apart in the corral. Only a tiny white fleck under the forelock might read as a star. However, the background is European.
